title: 2016-20 Pilot 6-speed: "Transmission Temperature Too Hot" with no codes, PGM-FI update and 3x ATF flush
summary: Honda Service Bulletin 23-073: worn ATF foams and thins under long high-load driving, cutting cooler flow and triggering the transmission temperature warning. Fix is a PGM-FI software update and three drain-and-fills with ATF DW-1, with the level checked hot.

specs.name: Fill per drain
specs.value: 3.3 US qt (3.1 L) ATF DW-1 (2WD and AWD)

specs.name: Washers
specs.value: Drain plug washer 90471-PX4-000 (18 mm), filler sealing washer 11107-PWA-300 (24 mm), new on the final fill

steps.text: Do an all-DTC check. Any codes: the bulletin doesn't apply. None: update the PGM-FI software (battery support connected the whole time), then clear any codes the update set.
Run the engine at 3,000 rpm in Park or Neutral until the radiator fan comes on, then let it idle. Shut it off on the lift.
Remove the filler bolt, drain the ATF, reinstall the drain plug with its washer at 49 N·m (36 lb-ft), fill 3.3 qt (3.1 L) of ATF DW-1, filler bolt at 44 N·m (32 lb-ft), and check the level.

Wheels off the ground, engine running, VSA off: from Drive, accelerate to 50 mph so it shifts through the first three gears into 4th and the converter locks up. Brake the front wheels to a stop, shift to Reverse, then Neutral. Do this five times in all.
Repeat the drain, fill and shifting routine once more, then drain a third time and refill with new washers on the drain plug and filler bolt.

Check the level hot (176 °F / 80 °C). A cold reading shows low or at the bottom dot; topping up to the top dot cold overfills it and brings the foaming back. Reset the Maintenance Minder as appropriate.

body: Honda says to use only genuine ATF DW-1 and to avoid aftermarket flush machines. "Flush" in this bulletin means repeated drain-and-fill.

sources.title: Service Bulletin 23-073: 2016-20 Pilot: Transmission Temp Too Hot Message on the MID
sources.citation: Symptom, cause and parts p. 1; warranty and software p. 2; repair procedure pp. 3-4; NHTSA ID 10242219
